question: Should OpenClaw add a default-off `tools.exec.pty` config default for non-sandbox exec, or keep PTY as a per-call-only tool parameter?
rationale: The missing behavior is source-reproducible, but the fix adds a new global shell-exec config surface that intersects security, sandbox, approval, and operator-control expectations.

options.title: Approve Narrow Config Default
options.body: Add `tools.exec.pty` as an optional default with unchanged false default, per-call override precedence, gateway approval coverage, and sandbox suppression coordination.

options.title: Keep Per-Call Only
options.body: Avoid another exec config knob and improve docs, skill guidance, or model instructions for commands that require PTY.

options.title: Defer For Exec Policy Review
options.body: Hold the request until maintainers settle broader exec configuration and PTY policy direction alongside the sandbox warning behavior.

recommendation.title: Approve Narrow Config Default
recommendation.body: Add `tools.exec.pty` as an optional default with unchanged false default, per-call override precedence, gateway approval coverage, and sandbox suppression coordination.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest history on original exec PTY support and adjacent fallback behavior.
